title: Top-up Deposits for a Declined Domain Auto-Renewal — Harborline Customer Accounts
content:
# Top-up deposits for a declined domain auto-renewal

> Harborline Customer Accounts

This policy sets the amount of the top-up deposit a holder makes so that account credit pays the next retry of a domain auto-renewal that the card declined. The top-up is the holder's own money placed on their own account credit, which the retry then draws on. Charges of any other holding, such as another domain's, are not counted by the top-up.

**Conditions of any deposit.** A deposit may be accepted only while the account status is active, a single deposit must be at least the tier's minimum deposit and at most the tier's maximum per transaction and must use one of the tier's deposit methods, a bank transfer must be at least the tier's bank transfer minimum, and a deposit that would raise the credit balance above the tier's maximum credit balance is refused in full, never accepted in part.

## When the top-up deposit is worked out

The top-up deposit is worked out only after the credit ledger carries a goodwill entry for the active subscription of the customer's most recent initial certificate issuance whenever that certificate was issued more than eleven calendar days after the subscription's documents were complete and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

The top-up deposit is not fixed until the credit ledger carries a goodwill entry for the account's only security-change notice of the last two months whenever that notice followed the decision of the account's most recent approved recovery request, decided within those two months, the account's sign-in shows the change that request asked for, and the notice came more than one day after the request's waiting period ended, and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

Before the top-up deposit is worked out, the credit ledger must carry a goodwill entry for the most recent domain refund line returned to account credit whenever no other such refund line shares its date, its refund credit entry was posted more than three calendar days after it, and the account's goodwill entries dated after the same calendar date one year before today total less than the tier's yearly goodwill limit.

## Making the deposit

The top-up deposit is the account holder's own payment of money into their own Harborline account credit from one of their own payment methods: their card, their PayPal account or their bank transfer. The agent unlocks the customer-side tool `make_topup_deposit_c7a3772f` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. One run records one deposit: the payment is taken from the holder's chosen method, the account credit balance goes up by the amount deposited, and the deposit is recorded on the account's credit history with its funding method. The holder sees the deposit and the higher balance at once, and the credit is available for any Harborline charge, including auto-renewals that try account credit.

## What the tool takes

| Parameter | What it is | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `account_id` | The reference number of the holder's Harborline account, as shown on the account record opened for this customer. | Identifier, as shown on the record |
| `funding_method` | How the holder pays the deposit. | One of `card` (charged to the holder's payment card), `paypal` (paid from the holder's PayPal account), `bank_transfer` (arrives by the holder's bank transfer); `none` is not a funding method for a deposit and is never the value for this tool |
| `amount` | The amount deposited, in US dollars. | A positive figure with 2 decimal places; any further decimals are rounded half up to the cent |

## What the tool returns

A completed run returns a line beginning "Deposit recorded", stating the reference number of the new deposit entry, the amount deposited in US dollars with two decimals, the funding method used and the account's new credit balance in US dollars with two decimals. The run is refused with an error line when `amount` is not a positive US dollar figure, or when `funding_method` is not `card`, `paypal` or `bank_transfer`.
